NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MCRCA No. 1208 of 2023  Madhusudan Tulsyan S/o Shri Sajjan Kumar Agrawal, Aged About 43 Years  Caste Marwadi, Occupation - Businessman (Saree Suhag Centre), R/o Village  Dhaura Tikra, Police Station And Tehsil Baikunthpur, District Korea  Chhattisgarh.

---- APPLICANT  Versus 1. State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer, Baikunthpur, District  Korea, (Wrongly Mentioned As M.C.B) Chhattisgarh.
2. Mahesh Prasad Sahu S/o Late Devkinandan Sahu Aged About 60 Years  R/o Village And Tehsil- Baikunthpur, District: Koriya (Baikunthpur),
 Chhattisgarh  --- RESPONDENTS _____________________________________________________________ For Applicant : Mr. Dhirendra Prasad Mishra, Advocate.

For State/ Respondent : Mr. Avinash K.
M i s h r a ,
 
G o v t .
 
A d v o c a t e ________________________________________________________ Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 19.10.2023 1.

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail, who has apprehension of being arrested in connection with Crime No. 129 of 2023, registered at Police Station- Baikunthpur, District Korea (CG) for the offence punishable under Sections 420 IPC.
2.

The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn in MCRCA No. 756 of 2023 on 09.08.2023, there is change of circumstances as the applicant has already been paid Rs.
3,00,000/- to the complainant on 12.09.2023.
3.

The prosecution case in brief is that a sale deed was executed between the applicant and the complainant for purchase of house to the tune of Rs. 46,00,000/- for which the complainant has paid Rs. 3,00,000 as advance subsequently, the applicant denied to purchase the same and did not return the money to the complainant, thereby, the offence has been committed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
He would further submit that the applicant has already paid the amount and has made the default good, therefore, the applicant may be granted benefit of anticipatory bail.
5. In pursuance of direction given by this Court the applicant has arrayed the complainant as respondent No.2.
The complainant appeared before this Court through DLSA Koriya and admitted the fact that Rs. 3,00,000/- has been paid to him by the applicant.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the anticipatory bail application.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
8.

Considering the fact that the applicant has already made good the default and paid Rs.
3,00,000/- to the complaint, I am inclined to extend the benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. to the applicant.

9. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is allowed and It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.

Sd/-
